newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Jan 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Jan 14.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Tuesday:

- The Supreme Court argument that unfolded on Monday over whether Paula Jones can proceed with her sexual harassment lawsuit against President Clinton found the Justices openly troubled by the prospect of a president having to defend himself in court while he is in office.
- President Clinton is drafting a budget that would set firm limits on Federal Medicaid spending as a way to help balance the budget by 2002.
- Seven men today were awarded the Medals of Honour that they were denied after World War II because they were black.
- A day after two of four female cadets withdrew from the Citidel, saying they had been harassed, the head of the college expressed his determination to make coeducation work.

- In a widening campaign of terror against an Arabic language newspaper in London owned by a Saudi prince, two mail clerks were injured when one of four letter bombs addressed to the newspaper exploded.
- The Food and Drug administration proposed to ban Seldane, a widely prescribed antihistamine because of rare but potentially deadly side effects.
